source.title: Helping a Marketing Agency Scale
source.transcript_source: Automatic captions via the community ask-hormozi corpus

inputs.business: An agency connects brands and marketing agencies with influencers and also manages influencers.
facts: Revenue grew from about $250,000 to $1 million in a year.
Customers have arrived organically through word of mouth.
Both brands and influencers benefit from keeping successful relationships private rather than referring competitors.
The owner struggles to reach more brands and influencers and has considered advertising but has not started.
The owner reports roughly $900,000 profit on $1 million revenue; accounting details are not available.

reference.diagnosis: Reliance on limited word of mouth prevents predictable acquisition on both sides of the agency.
reference.action: Test paid acquisition using an existing influencer's success story and a clear offer; establish a repeatable motion beyond referrals.
reference.caution: Advertising economics and delivery capacity are not established; a controlled test is more defensible than a promise to scale.

source.title: Helping an Online Service Business Get to $5M/Year
source.transcript_source: Automatic captions via the community ask-hormozi corpus

inputs.business: Two golf coaches run a consumer coaching subscription alongside a sponsorship-funded media business.
facts: Social content attracts substantial traffic and brands willing to pay for exposure.
Sponsorship revenue is growing and currently supports the business.
Subscription revenue has declined; total revenue fell from about $2.6 million to $1.4 million.
The founders are passionate about coaching and believe the membership could become the larger business.
The owner identifies poor data and divided focus as problems and would like to sell the business eventually.
unknowns: Revenue and contribution profit split by business line

reference.diagnosis: The founders divide effort between a shrinking subscription and a growing media business while favoring the weaker line.
reference.action: Prioritize the growing sponsorship/media business and create more free golf content to expand attention and monetization.
reference.caution: The recommendation reflects the consultation, not proof that media will outperform; business-line economics still need validation.

source.title: I Built a $1.5M Business I Secretly Hate
source.transcript_source: Automatic captions via the community ask-hormozi corpus

inputs.business: A specialist builds custom solutions in customers' own cloud accounts, then sells ongoing managed services.
facts: A custom implementation can take roughly 18 months before ongoing managed services begin.
The founder is the trusted specialist and delivery depends heavily on their work.
Demand arrives when buyers learn the founder exists, but there are too few people to deliver.
There is no predictable hiring pipeline for similarly skilled specialists.
The owner is weighing expansion of custom builds against selling managed services for infrastructure they did not build.
unknowns: Margins and retention for each offering

reference.diagnosis: Long custom implementations and founder dependence constrain entry into the recurring managed-service business.
reference.action: Try a smaller paid assessment and high-impact improvement to existing cloud infrastructure, followed by managed services; reduce the lengthy front-end build requirement.
reference.caution: Hiring is a plausible contributing constraint. The reference emphasizes changing the front-end offer; a label match alone cannot validate the recommendation.
